details:
Whilst the addition of Copy/Paste to the keyboard is welcome in [1220], there may be times when a world developer wishes to initiate a copy for text data via udon.
 —
# Examples
1. A world developer has user persistent data. They wish for the user to save this user persistent data without potential for error, such as deletion of text using the on-screen keyboard. As such, they provide a "Copy" button, that when pressed, writes to the clipboard, allowing the user to paste the data elsewhere for storage.
2. A user has a video player. However, they wish to improve Quest compatibility by providing a "URL converter" that takes popular media links and converts them to a link-resolver equivalent, as is common. Rather than risk the user accidentally back-spacing portions of the URL which they cannot see within the VRCHAT keyboard, they intelligently convert and copy the new URL `on End Edit`, for the user to paste into a video player address bar.
3. A world developer is hosting an event. During this event, they wish to provide codes which are linked to a website for various event-related activities or interactions. Rather than force the user to exit VRChat unnecessarily by way of URL, they provide a menu in-world to copy the code(s) at any time, which can be pasted into a website at a later time.
 —
# Request
Please add support for the [GUIUtility.systemCopyBuffer](https://docs.unity3d.com/2019.4/Documentation/ScriptReference/GUIUtility-systemCopyBuffer.html), by adding a `GUIUtility set systemCopyBuffer` node, and write-only access to `GUIUtility.systemCopyBuffer` in U#.
 —
# Why Write-Only
Being aware of VRChat's concerns with general purpose input/output (GPIO) from the VRC client, write-only access would require user-intervention to write back ("paste") clipboard contents in any particular world, and would be restricted to doing so in UI Input Fields and *re-implementations* thereof.
 
**Likewise**, write only access **prevents random-access of the user clipboard**, *which poses a security risk in the event the clipboard contains sensitive content.*
 —
# Further considerations
**If random-write access is of a concern, the Udon implementation could provide a mandatory UI dialog prompting the user if they wish to to copy text to the clipboard.**
E.G. "*Do you wish to copy "Some random text that will be truncated..." [509 Characters] to the clipboard?*" with "`Cancel`" & "`Copy`" options.
**Likewise, a variable indicating the copy's success could be provided, allowing udon developers to handle copy failure.**
E.G. `GUIUtility set systemCopyBuffer` will return a bool indicating the success (true) or failure (false) based on whether the user copied or canceled the action.
title: Add Write-Only Access to Clipboard (systemCopyBuffer)
